knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A PV array generates whenever light falls on it, so it is treated as live for the whole job, including when the mains is off.
Energy Safe Victoria guidance (reviewed 15 April 2025) says DC supply cables from the array can still be live after the power is switched off.
No official source reviewed in this draft confirms that switching off the inverter makes the array safe, so the safe rule is to treat the array as live.

Energy Safe Victoria guidance (reviewed 15 April 2025) describes isolation at the main switchboard with lock-out and tag-out, and treats PV installation and maintenance as licensed electrical installation work.
Energy Safe Victoria refers to AS/NZS 4836 for safe working on low-voltage installations. AS/NZS 1891.4 and the cleaning clauses of AS/NZS 5033 are not cited here.

practicalCriteria: The learner states, for a scenario, that the array is treated as live while light falls on it.
The learner keeps the spray away from marked connectors, junction boxes and inverters during a supervised demonstration.
The learner stops and refers on sight of exposed wiring or a burnt connector in a scenario, without touching the component.
The learner records the hazard observation with a photograph and a position.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation of a supervised scenario. A knowledge pass does not verify electrical hazard control on a live array.
evidenceRequired: Pre-clean hazard checklist with the live-array assumption recorded
Photographs and sketch marking connectors, junction boxes and cable runs
Stop and referral record for any electrical concern
Referral outcome from a licensed electrician or installer
stopWorkCriteria: The learner treats the array as dead because the mains or inverter is off.
The learner touches a cable or connector to test whether it is live.
The learner sprays water onto a junction box or inverter.
The learner offers to isolate or repair the system.
